title: park hardcodes the literal parked status

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`ops.park` defaults to the string `"parked"` and `tui.act` passes the same literal. Every
other status in the tool is configurable: `open_status`, `done_status` and
`retired_status` all live in config, and `retired_status` is even back-filled for projects
that predate it.

So a project whose vocabulary omits `parked` gets:

    $ slicer park S01
    slicer: unknown status 'parked'; known: ['done', 'open', 'retired']

from a command the help advertises, and the TUI's `p` key fails the same way. It fails
loudly rather than corrupting anything, which is why nobody noticed.

This is an invariant violation, not only a bug. `__init__.py` says nothing in the package
may hardcode a value belonging to one project, and `ARCHITECTURE.md` repeats it. A status
name is exactly that kind of value.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/config.py` — a `parked_status`, back-filled like `retired_status`
- `src/slicer/ops.py` — `park`
- `src/slicer/tui.py` — the `p` branch
- `src/slicer/cli.py` — the `park` subcommand

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `Park_ProjectWithoutParked_UsesTheConfiguredStatus`.
2. `Park_ProjectDeclaringNoParkedStatus_RefusesWithAClearMessage` — rather than naming a
   status the project never had.
3. `Tui_ParkKey_UsesTheConfiguredStatus`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Add `parked_status` to `Config`, defaulting to `"parked"`, back-filled on load exactly as
`retired_status` is — only that one key, so a project that deliberately dropped some other
status does not get it back. Then read it in `ops.park` and `tui.act`.

Where a project declares no parked status at all, refuse the way `retire` does when
`retired_status` is empty: name the config key rather than a status the project never had.

**Not in this slice:** a general mechanism for optional statuses. Three named ones is the
shape the tool has.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
A project whose statuses are only open and done gets a coherent message from both `park`
and the TUI.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body:
One commit: `parked_status` on `Config` (config.py), `ops.park` reading it,
the TUI `p` branch and the `park` CLI command routed through `ops.park`, and
tests in `test_park.py`.
